title: The Kawhi Anomaly
dek: The biggest rebound ever recorded by a 34-year-old.
home_dek: The biggest rebound ever recorded by a 34-year-old. Late surges usually fade. Which half of his will last?
teaser: The biggest rebound ever recorded by a 34-year-old.
lead: Kawhi Leonard went from a good starter to the fifth-best player in the league per minute, at 34. No player 34 or older has ever jumped that far in one season.
Eight players have surged to star level after 31. None kept three-quarters of the gain the next year. His bigger role usually lasts. His hot shooting usually doesn't.
findings: The biggest one-year jump ever by a player 34 or older, and the only star since 1978 to set career highs in usage and true shooting in the same season after 33.
Eight players surged to star level after 31. None kept three-quarters of the improvement the next season.
His bigger role usually lasts; his hot shooting usually doesn't. The forecast: an impact of +1.31 next season, roughly a top-ten level.

social.hook: Kawhi Leonard went from a good starter to the fifth-best player in the league per minute, at 34. No player 34 or older has ever jumped that far in one season.
points: Late surges have an unkind history. Eight players surged to star level after 31. None kept three-quarters of the improvement the next season.
His surge came in two parts: a heavier role and hotter shooting. His bigger role usually lasts. His hot shooting usually doesn't.

title: The Queta Problem
dek: Why he’s a top-50 player, and why 2026-27 proves it.
teaser: Twice waived, 39th pick, #41 in The 644. Why he's a top-50 player.
kicker: Article №2 · Trust the data · revised v2

social.hook: Neemias Queta was waived twice and picked 39th. Our ranking puts him #41 of 644, a full tier above his reputation.
points: His workload grew nearly 6× (333 → 1,926 minutes) and his efficiency went up anyway.
We attacked our own number twice. Of 33 comparable big-man seasons since 2020, 39% delivered a top-50-caliber follow-up.
We wrote down in advance what counts as being wrong: #51–70 is a near miss, below #70 a clean miss.

title: The Rise and Fall of Ja Morant
teaser: From the 97th percentile to 79 of 246 games.
kicker: Article №1 · A career autopsy · revised v2

social.hook: Ja Morant went from the 97th percentile of the league in 2021-22 to playing 79 of 246 games since 2023.
points: Of his shooting collapse, 88% was shot-making, not shot selection.
His three-point slump covers 20-of-85 attempts: too few to tell decline from variance.
The one split that moved beyond doubt went up: his free throws, to .897.
Our verdict: #140 is a defensible price for the delivery risk. It is probably the wrong forecast of the talent.
